title: August and the Clock
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, 1897, Silas Ravensworth — a pearl diver's son indentured to the Halloway Trading Company — has spent his life keeping his head down and his ledgers clean. When an infant is abandoned at the company door with a note ordering him to forget the child's face, Silas recognizes the mark on the swaddling cloth as belonging to a drowned diver's family, victims of a company-ordered dive in lethal waters. With the help of Odile Marchetti, a court stenographer risking her career, and the found-family of dockworkers who raised him, Silas races to gather testimony from surviving divers before the company's hired historians can bury the truth in official record. The climax comes at the admiralty inquiry, where Silas trades his own freedom — breaking his indenture contract publicly — to enter the testimony into evidence; the epilogue finds him freed, the child adopted by the dock community, and the company's directors facing ruin as the true history enters the record.
about_author: E. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers and indenture contracts from colonial-era trading companies. Their fiction draws on the marginalia of those records — the names struck through, the deaths logged as weather.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Silas Ravensworth, POV. A day in the life at Halloway Trading Company: Silas audits pearl shipments, endures the overseer's contempt, and visits the dock families who informally raised him after his father's diving death. Establishes his careful invisibility and quiet grief. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Left at the Door
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. At closing time he finds an infant on the company step, wrapped in cloth bearing a diver's clan-mark, with a note: 'Forget this face.' The night watchman saw nothing. Silas hides the child rather than report it, knowing what the company does to inconvenient things. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Clan-Mark
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. He brings the swaddling cloth to old Maren, a retired diver who identifies the mark as belonging to the Okonkwo family — three divers lost last spring in waters the company certified safe. Silas realizes the child survived a family the ledger lists as 'weather losses.' Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: A Stenographer's Hours
chapters.summary: Odile Marchetti, POV. Odile transcribes company depositions by day and notices patterns: identical testimony from witnesses who never met. She crosses paths with Silas when he comes asking, discreetly, about inquiry procedures. Two cautious people recognize each other's caution. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Omits
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Using his access to company records, Silas discovers the safety report for the fatal dive was altered — the depth warnings struck out in a hand matching Director Halloway's. He copies nothing yet, but memorizes everything. Emotional beat: the vertigo of knowing too much.

chapters.title: The Dock Family
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. The dockworkers quietly take in the baby, naming her August for the month she arrived. Maren reflects on every diver the sea and the company have taken, and decides this child will not be one more erased name. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing around a cradle.

chapters.title: Questions in Safe Waters
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. He begins interviewing surviving divers under cover of routine inventory checks. One, Tomas Okonkwo's old partner, admits they were ordered down past safe depth to reach a newly charted bed — and that he was paid to keep silent. Emotional beat: guilt and courage wrestling.

chapters.title: The Historian Arrives
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The company retains Mr. Aldous Crane, a celebrated chronicler, to write its official history ahead of the admiralty inquiry. Odile watches him charm the clerks and realize he is not recording history — he is manufacturing it. Emotional beat: dread of a polished lie.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Archive
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Crane offers Silas promotion and freedom from his indenture if he hands over the archive keys and forgets the child. Silas refuses, and knows he has just marked himself. That night someone searches his room. Emotional beat: the cost of refusal made tangible.

chapters.title: Testimony in Whispers
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Odile secretly transcribes the divers' statements in her own shorthand, hiding pages inside finished deposition folios. She and Silas build a chain of custody: each witness signs, each page dated. Emotional beat: fragile hope taking physical form.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Recants
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The paid-off diver withdraws his statement after his daughter's job at the company is threatened. Silas watches a man choose survival over truth and cannot hate him. The chain weakens; two testimonies remain. Emotional beat: despair tempered by understanding.

chapters.title: Crane's Draft
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. Odile is assigned to type Crane's manuscript and reads the official version: the Okonkwos died of their own recklessness, the depths exaggerated by superstitious natives. She copies key discrepancies between his text and the raw logs. Emotional beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: August Learns to Laugh
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. A quieter chapter: the dock community's rhythms with the baby at its center, Silas learning to be held by people again, and Maren telling him he was never meant to carry this alone. Emotional beat: tenderness as fuel for the fight ahead.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Ledgers
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. The company discovers the altered safety report has been noticed; they forge a replacement and plan to charge Silas with falsification. His only defense is the original page — which he must steal from the director's private safe before the inquiry opens. Emotional beat: cornered animal calm.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Record
chapters.summary: Silas and Odile, alternating. During the director's banquet, Odile creates a diversion while Silas cracks the safe and photographs the original report with a borrowed camera plate. They escape through the coal chute as alarms rise. Emotional beat: terror transformed into triumph.

chapters.title: Hunted
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Warrants issue for Silas — theft, breach of indenture, kidnapping of the child. The dock families scatter August to safe houses. Odile burns her shorthand originals after having them witnessed by a notary sympathetic to the divers. Emotional beat: sacrifice deepening on all sides.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Opens
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The admiralty inquiry convenes; Crane presents the company's seamless history. The presiding examiner seems inclined to accept it until an anonymous package delivers the photographed original report. The room turns. Emotional beat: the first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Silas Speaks
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Summoned in irons, Silas tears up his own indenture contract before the court, declaring that no man bound by Halloway can testify freely — then testifies anyway, naming the altered report, the depth orders, and the payment for silence. Emotional beat: freedom claimed at the moment of greatest peril.

chapters.title: The Divers Take the Stand
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. One by one, divers testify despite threats; even the recanting witness returns, bringing his daughter to hear him tell the truth. Crane's manuscript collapses under cross-examination. Emotional beat: ordinary people choosing courage together.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Odile, POV. The inquiry rules the deaths were caused by company orders; criminal referrals follow. Halloway resigns in disgrace; Crane's history is withdrawn and reissued with corrections he did not write. Silas's charges are dismissed, his indenture voided. Emotional beat: justice arriving imperfectly but arriving.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Silas, POV. Silas visits the divers' memorial wall and adds three names the company never carved. He offers Odile not gratitude but partnership — she accepts. The victors' historians got there second. Emotional beat: grief finally given shape and honor.

chapters.title: August and the Clock
chapters.summary: Maren, POV, one year later. On August's first birthday, the dock community gathers; Silas, now keeper of an independent archive of divers' testimony, gives the child a small clock that runs backward — so she'll always know time can be turned toward the truth. Emotional beat: peace earned, future open.
